title: Staff one factory from Production
summary: With the game linked, each factory in Supply › Production's factory staffing has a Staff this site button. It hires and reassigns the factory workers that factory needs and writes its week into the game, with Undo, the way a shop's Staffing already could.

title: Staff every station every hour your shop opens
summary: A staffed shop with complete demand data has a third staffing plan beside the demand plan and Full cover 24/7: Every open hour. It puts somebody on every station for every hour the shop already opens, whatever the demand, and never changes its opening hours.

title: Play with Alcware Seasons and other mods
summary: A modded save now says which mods the board reads in a line under the clock: Economy Expansion, Retail Expansion, a Dynamic Rivals rival count, and the Alcware Seasons season and day. With Seasons' seasonal demand on, Open a store predicts sales at this season's demand for the 27 products the mod changes.

title: Track your place on the Rivals leaderboard
summary: See your rank among the rivals by weekly income, how far you lead or trail the best rival, and how many days in a row you have held first place. It appears as a figure on the Overview and a block on Milestones, worked out from your save without opening the game's Rivals app. Hide it under Preferences if you do not need it.

title: Suggest features from the voting list
summary: Submit a public idea from the voting dialog, with no account or save needed. Suggestions include your vote and let other visitors support them; votes help prioritise work without promising delivery.

title: Use Big Copilot in Italian
summary: Italian now includes a complete set of machine-drafted interface translations. Choose Italiano under Language to use them, and help improve the wording through the community translation page. Community-selected wording takes precedence over these drafts.

title: Plan expansion in buildings you already rent
summary: Business and factory expansion plans now suggest empty buildings you already rent alongside new rentals. Already rented locations need no second deposit, and a factory's starter depot can use an empty rented warehouse too.

title: Help translate Big Copilot
summary: Find wording in English or your language, suggest a correction or vote for an existing version from your browser. A single contribution can improve the wording, with no account needed. Italian is open for contributions too.

title: Account for renovated building sizes
summary: Supported Alcware renovation records now supply the building size used by the dashboard and campaign planner. Campaign advice pauses when its calculation does not match the save. The dashboard also supports current building and marketing values from Game Link 0.5, with downloadable snapshots that retain those values; this path requires the updated Link mod.

title: Measure staffing demand in shops and offices
summary: Staffing now remembers demand separately for each company and business. Plan a temporary measurement using spare capacity or one extra station where it can help, then confirm that staffing and stock stayed available. Confirmed demand stays stable when you change the schedule. Office plans preserve cleaning and other duties, and account for employee weekly limits. Missing customer reports remain unknown rather than being treated as zero demand.

title: Plan a factory in all seven UI languages
summary: Plan a factory, custom product setups, recent production findings and the bug-report form now have text in German, Spanish, French, Korean, Portuguese, Russian and Turkish. The latest cinema capacity advice and staffing labels are included too. These translations are machine drafts and remain open for native-language review.

title: See what holds back a cinema
summary: A cinema held below its building capacity by installed equipment now names the screens, projection booths, ticket kiosks or concessions stand registers that limit it. Its hours show a warning with advice to add the limiting equipment and staff any new employee stations. A cinema at its actual building capacity keeps the neutral reading.

title: Cinema and theatre floor plans in the finder
summary: The finder now shows all six cinema and theatre layouts, including their stepped seating areas. Filter cinemas and theatres by layout and open a building to see its plan before choosing where to rent.

title: Plan a factory with any mix of products
summary: Custom setup in Plan a factory lets you combine any factory products and choose the machine count for each. Search by product or workstation, then follow the five steps with the combined ingredients, storage, staffing and investment. A new factory starts empty; one you run starts from its current machines. Each saved plan keeps its own selection. Demand combines measured sales across your shops, with no guessed demand for products you have not sold.

title: Report a bug from the page, with your save
summary: Report a bug in the footer, in Help & feedback and beside Could not read the save opens a short form. Describe what went wrong, and tick Attach my save and Attach technical details if you want to. Your text becomes a public issue on GitHub, and the form links to it. The save and the full error are never published. They are kept privately for 30 days and used only to fix the bug. If the report cannot be sent, the form points to the Discord support channel instead.

title: Plan a factory: from what to make to production, step by step
summary: Expansion › Plan a factory now walks a factory plan through five steps: What, Where, Investment, Until production and Running. Pick the shops it supplies and, in For, a new factory or one you already run. What is the planner you know, with each product's machines sized to your shops' peak day, a warning when a line stays short of what they take, and the surplus valued as an export at the game's own export price. Where lists every warehouse building to rent, cheapest first, with its parking for trucks and its deposit. Investment is the one-off cost: the machines and pallet shelves at list price, the installation firm or a delivery, the deposit and a Freight Truck T1, with an optional bank loan; raw material, wages and rent a week are shown beside it as running costs. Until production is a checklist ticked from your save, with buttons for hiring and weekly import amounts when the game is linked. Running compares output with the plan once the factory works. For a factory you run, the steps cover only what the change adds. Businesses › Results now also counts a depot's and a factory's own vehicles in what was invested.

title: Plan a factory: add the products a type can also sell
summary: Expansion › Plan a factory now has Add product under the range. It lists what the business type can also stock beyond its main products, such as umbrellas or soda at a Florist, each with the game's own weight for that type. An added product gets its own line, with machines, output, raw material and the weekly ingredient order like the main products, and × takes it out again. If every shop of the type already sells it, the line uses what they sell; otherwise you type an estimate a shop sells a day, which starts from what your shops sell of it or, if none do, from your main products' rate times the weight. Your additions are kept per type.

title: Factories: what your shops sell against what each line makes
summary: Supply › Production and each factory's page have a Sold / day column: what the shops a line supplies actually sell a day, next to what it makes and ships. When a line cannot keep up even round the clock, its status reads short: needs N more machines, and the tip says what that gives, for example 1 more machine makes 9,600 a day against 5,066 needed. Every short now says what is short: hours, the ingredient order, or production, each as its own chip, so a short order is no longer read as a short line. A factory with a line short of machines opens under Needs a change.

title: Open a new store: plan it, open it, and watch it earn the investment back
summary: Expansion has a new view, Open a store. Pick a type from the neighbourhoods with the most demand, from any type, or from a Demand cell's new Open a store here, then pick the building in Find a location, fixed to that type. The board lists everything a fully outfitted store of that type needs in that building: what the type requires to open, an item for each customer demand, enough tills for the building's capacity and shelving copied from your own store of the same layout, with the installation firm's price or, for self-installation, a shopping list by furniture store on the map, and the deposit. It then estimates the profit a day from the game's own rules for customers, prices, demand and wages, with the best marketing mix, and shows how many days it takes to earn the investment back, as a range, after tax, against what your own stores of that type earn, and with an optional bank loan. Offices are estimated too; cinemas and theatres show the investment only. A checklist then follows the store until it opens, ticking itself from the save: the lease, furniture, staff for the opening hours, uniforms, customer demands, marketing and logistics, with buttons to staff the store, assign uniforms and set the cheapest marketing mix through the game link. Once the store trades, the plan compares itself with it: the investment, the profit a day and the first days against the plan, the share paid back, the day it breaks even, and any loan it was planned with. Your plans are kept per character, opened stores included. Businesses › Results also has a Payback column: for each shop, office and chain, the day its setup was earned back or how many days are still to go, with the same line on a business's own page.

title: Staff a site in one step, and undo it in one
summary: A shop's or an office's Staffing has Staff this site, and Staffing › Staff needs has Staff all sites. One review hires the best candidates, moves spare staff across, and writes the new week at every site it reaches, including sites that only need new hours; each site then says whether its week was written. Pick Hire and schedule, Hire only (assigned with no hours, as at a headquarters or a warehouse) or Schedule only; Quick hire works the same way. A shop you put on full cover 24/7 is staffed around the clock. With Big Copilot Link 0.4.0 it all goes to the game in one step, and one Undo takes back every hire, move and week, until the game's next day. Older versions of the mod still hire, then write the other weeks one by one, without undo.

title: Marketing: the cheapest campaigns for 100% promotion, set in one click
summary: Every shop and office page now shows the cheapest set of marketing campaigns that brings its promotion to 100%, or its marketing to 100% where the street's foot traffic can't get it there, with the cost per day before and after. With the Big Copilot Link mod 0.4.0 one click books it in the game, for one site or all of them at once, and adds a switch for every campaign type to the business's BizMan Marketing page, so no phone call or chat with the agency is needed. Campaigns a business already has switch on or off at any time; a new campaign type is added through a marketing agency already in your phone's contacts while it is open, and the board says when an agency opens or which one to visit first. The overview lists the sites that could reach more promotion or pay less for it. Undo puts the campaigns back as they were.

title: A new layout: problems first, and a sidebar with five places to fix them
summary: The board is rebuilt around what needs your attention. The Overview opens on Needs attention, each finding with a button that takes you to the exact setting, and a way back to where you were. A sidebar on the left holds five places, the open one with its views under it: the Overview, Businesses (results, cash and loans, prices against the market, a standards comparison with uniforms you can set from it, milestones), Supply (the changes to make, imports, deliveries, production, and a goods flow you can drag and zoom like the map), Staffing (schedules, staff needs, payroll) and Expansion (demand, finding a location, planning a factory), then the City map and the Wiki. The button at its foot folds the sidebar to a strip of icons, and the board remembers it. Every business page links to its schedule, deliveries and prices. Changes you mark, apply through the game link, or that a later save confirms now look different, and preferences and help sit under the one ··· menu at the sidebar's foot. Old links keep working.

title: Big Copilot in your language
summary: The footer's Game names setting is now Language, and it translates the whole page: Big Copilot comes in German, Spanish, French, Portuguese and Russian as well as English, with the game's names to match. The game's other languages still change the game's names, and the rest of the page stays English. Your choice is kept for your next visit. Most of the Spanish, French, Portuguese and Russian is machine-translated for now; if you speak one of them, the link under the picker shows how to help check it.

title: Hire and place staff for every site at once
summary: Company › Payroll is now Staff. It adds up what each shop, office and factory still needs by role, moves spare people between sites first, and picks the most skilled of your headhunters' candidates, with filters for the demands you want to avoid. One confirm hires them, puts them at their sites and writes their hours, through the Big Copilot Link mod 0.3.0. Hires cannot be undone.

title: Goods flow you can read on a phone
summary: On a phone or a portrait tablet, Supply's goods-flow diagram is now a chain you read top to bottom: your importers, depots, factories and shops in the order the goods travel, with the pipes between them. A depot's shops fold into one card from four up, the sites worth a look sit in a row on top, and shops no pipe reaches share one line at the bottom. Tap a site to follow it: what comes in, what goes out, the pipe carrying a short or stalled product in colour, its problems in words, and one tap to its rows or its site page. With no pipe yet, the box says so and links the wiki's guide to imports.

title: Game names in the language you play in
summary: A new Game names setting in the footer, beside Theme, shows the game's own names in any language the game ships: items, business types, neighbourhoods, stations, skills and staff demands, on the board, inside its findings and in the wiki, so the board reads like your game. The rest of the page stays English. Search finds a name in either language, and lists sort in the language you picked. If your browser prefers one of the game's languages, the board asks once whether to use it.

title: Floor plans for every building, and a Layout filter
summary: Each building the finder lists now names its layout, the game's short code for its shape, such as C1 or H3. Click a building on the map or in the list and its card shows the game's own floor plan for it, with its entrances (loading bays for a warehouse). A new Layout filter in Find a location lists only the layouts you pick, and a saved search keeps it.

title: Supply by shop, warehouse and factory, and staffing for factory lines
summary: Supply is now three tabs, one per object: Shops, Warehouses and Factories. Each opens on what needs a change, with the figure to type beside the setting it changes and a tick at the head of the row; one checklist under the tabs counts your ticks across all three and copies what is left. Idle stock folds into one row per warehouse or per cause, a shelf topped up far above what it sells gets a lower target to type, and the goods-flow diagram is a view of each tab: click a site to see its rows. Factories shows the hours each line is rostered against the hours it needs, 24/7 or for what your shops use, and too few hours is a change to type. A new Staffing for factory lines block gives each line's shifts, the factory workers the plan needs against those you have, and what the difference does to your wages. This answers the voted request "Supply chain for factories not running 24/7".

title: Size supply for 24/7 or for demand, and find stock no plan sends on
summary: Supply now judges every item once and uses the same word for it everywhere: covered, tight, short, no plan, paused, stalled, idle, made here or new. A Sizing switch on Orders, on the factory and import checks and on each warehouse and factory page sizes your factory lines, top-ups and imports for 24/7 rated output or for what your shops actually use, with one 15% margin over the whole chain from import to sale and figures rounded up to tens. Under Demand, a shop open less than a week is projected forward and marked "may still be ramping". Tight means an order covers the use but not the margin; it shows on Supply and never on Today. Shops and warehouses stocked by a repeating wholesale contract are judged against it. A new Not routed finding points at stock in a warehouse or factory that no plan sends on while your own shops sell it.

title: Every site has its own page, and you can search the board
summary: Each shop, warehouse, factory and office now opens as its own page with an address, so a reload keeps it and Back and Forward walk between sites; a crumb takes you back to where you came from, and site names on Today, Supply and the map link to it. Press / or Ctrl+K to search the whole board: pages, your sites, products, kinds of finding, location presets and the game's help pages, with everyday words like hire, debt or difficulty. Today has an Ask the board row whose questions land on the answer. The difficulty you play on sits beside the clock, and Company › Results can show your week by weekday.

title: Write to the game from the board (Big Copilot Link 0.2.0)
summary: With the Big Copilot Link mod 0.2.0, the board can now make three changes in your game for you: set uniforms where roles have none, apply the import amounts from Plan imports, and write a shop's staffing plan, for one shop or a run of shops. Every change shows what the game will do before you apply it, can be undone once, and is refused, with nothing written, if the game has moved on since the board last read it. The first write from a browser asks for approval in the game; after that it is remembered.

title: Fix: warehouses fed by your own factory no longer read as short
summary: A warehouse your own factory tops up every morning on a logistics route was flagged as a critical import shortfall for every item the factory delivers, often with an alert that weekly orders cannot cover their week and a large one-off to bring in. The board now counts what your factories bring on routes before it judges the import, so a backup import next to such a route no longer raises the alarm, paused or not. If a route brings only part of what leaves, the import is sized on the rest, and a busy day that could still empty the shelf before the next morning's round is still flagged. The Factories page takes the same routes into account.

title: Full cover for a new shop, and a demand plan after 9 days
summary: A new shop can now run a demand test: the Staffing block offers Full cover 24/7 beside its usual plan, every serving station staffed every hour with the fewest people the game's rules allow, and a step to open every day 0 to 24. Nine days after the shop's first customer the board has the shop's own week and gives it the demand plan, without waiting two weeks. Hours nobody came count as no customers. When the data is in and the shop is still fully staffed, the Staffing block and Today say to switch to the demand plan. Plans now say in one step how many people to add: who to assign from your unassigned staff and how many to hire, and hire counts are the true minimum.

title: Imports that read Smart Delivery, and your own order figures
summary: The weekly imports now understand the purchasing agent's Smart Delivery setting: its amount is a stock level the agent tops up to each Monday, not a delivery, and the board judges it that way, in the order the game delivers your contracts. The imports table shows what arrived last week, what is set in game ("in stock" or "a week"), and a Set to box with the board's suggestion that you can change. Your figures carry into the Plan imports checklist, which names the importer to change when a material has more than one contract. For Smart Delivery the suggestion is the stock that runs everything the depot feeds at full capacity for a week, so it only moves when your capacity does.

title: No more gas station tips
summary: Big Copilot will no longer tell you to open a gas station. Or a wholesaler. Or a casino. The city runs those itself and is not selling, however good the numbers look. Market demand and Find a location now suggest only business types you can actually open, straight from the game's own F1 help, including ones nobody in your city runs yet.

title: Link to the game
summary: A third way in beside the save folder and the single file: with the Big Copilot Link mod from the Steam Workshop enabled, click Link to the game and the board reads the running game itself. No folder to pick, and the board follows the game as you play: it refreshes on the game hour, after a game save, and whenever you click Update. The mod serves the game's own save to this page on your computer and to nothing else; Chrome and Edge ask once to allow the site to reach it. The local watcher learnt the same trick as --game.

title: Contributions welcome
summary: Help improve Big Copilot with fixes, features, docs or tests. The GitHub README now has a short contribution guide: focused PRs, mockups to discuss bigger ideas, test results and agent review for AI-written code.

title: Staffing, in hours and days you can act on
summary: The staffing plan now builds a week one person can really work. Nobody is spread across two businesses, hours stay inside the full-time band the game pays for, and somebody who asked for four days a week gets four, not five. A shop the board cannot read yet says so and covers its cleaning and security in the meantime, instead of offering to clear a schedule that nothing here could put back. The block is now called Staffing and speaks the game's own language: hours and days rather than shifts, entries you copy into BizMan one day at a time, stations by name with the short codes on hover, and people to hire rather than posts, each sized at the 30 hours a week a full-time employee is owed. It also says what makes its numbers worth reading, which is two weeks with every station staffed. Building capacity replaces "door cap" on the board and in the location finder.

title: A page for every site, and a week of staffing to copy in
summary: Every site's page now leads with the warnings about that site, and hovering one lights the part of the page that shows why. Shops and offices gain a profit rank among your trading sites, trend sparks and a cost bar, satisfaction against the 80 line with a lamp for each amenity, what pulls customers in, the ceiling each busy hour ran into, and a crew view that folds big rosters into one row per role. Depots and factories get pages of their own for the first time: a seven-day rail for each item with its delivery truck, what each depot feeds, a square for every machine filled by how much of the week it is staffed, and the inputs each line eats. A home opens from its map card. Shops also get Staffing: a week of hours to copy into BizMan, cut so that nobody works more than the 12 hours a day the game allows, people placed where their schedule demands hold, cleaning and security covered, and how many to hire for each station. Tick each entry off as you set it. The Optimize staffing card on Today opens the shop where it saves the most work. Gyms, hairdressers, theatres and nightclubs now get at-the-ceiling and overstaffed warnings, and switching a warning kind off moves its smaller findings to the bottom of the list and says so.

title: A Discord to talk it over in
summary: The footer's Follow column now links a Discord server for Big Ambitions and Big Copilot: somewhere to ask what a number means, compare saves and strategies, and say what the board should show next. The invite is in the footer on the landing screen and on the board, beside YouTube and the subreddit.

title: Choose light or dark
summary: The footer now has a theme control: match your system, or pin the board to light or dark. The choice is remembered in your browser and is applied before the page draws, so returning to it never flashes the other palette. Scrollbars and drop-downs follow the theme you picked instead of staying with your operating system's.

title: Warnings for unmet staff demands
summary: Needs attention now tells you when your employees' demands are not met, at every kind of site: the schedule they asked for, equipment at their desk, a water cooler or fridge in the building, a clean workplace. Each site gets one line naming what is missing and for how many staff, and health insurance and a happy boss go on one company line. The line turns critical once someone with an unmet demand has warned they will quit, and a site's page lists the demands under its crew.

title: Staffing by the hour for offices
summary: Law firms, travel agencies and the other office businesses now get the same Customers by hour grid as shops, with staff at computers as their capacity, and the same warnings when they sit at the ceiling or have staff standing idle. Offices form their own chain in the Portfolio and list their fee instead of shelves. The at-the-ceiling warning for shops and offices now names the right limit for each hour.

title: Save your location searches
summary: The location finder can keep its filters and sort as a named search. Saved searches sit in a new Saved row, are shared by all your characters and apply in one click. The finder also stays open when you visit another page and come back.

title: Sort the Supply tables
summary: Click a column header in Supply's stock checks, weekly imports or daily top-ups to sort by it, click again to reverse, or pick "usual order" to put the rows back. Imports and top-ups sort within each depot or factory.

title: Sort and filter premises by size
summary: The location finder shows each building's floor area as a sortable m² column, and a new Size filter narrows the rent, take-over and for-sale lists to a minimum and maximum m².

title: Find a location on the map
summary: The map gains a location finder: pick a kind and type, choose to rent, take over or buy, and get every available building ranked by neighbourhood demand and foot traffic, with estimated rent, deposit, door cap and rivals. Any building's card now shows its owner, renter, size, cap, traffic and rent. The Today card counts vacant units, a Growth cell jumps to premises for its type, and the Wiki explains how rent works.

title: Offices and fairer rankings in Market demand
summary: The By type grid now shows each business's average demand across its main products instead of a count of strong ones, so florists, cinemas and theaters are listed and ranked on the same scale. Law firms, travel agencies and the other office businesses appear in their own band, read from their hourly fee, with your own office outlined.

title: Compare your shop prices in the Wiki
summary: Business guides now show each shop's configured prices alongside neighbourhood market minimums, including products and services. Missing comparisons are explained, expired supply events no longer hide prices, and shops without a known neighbourhood keep their prices visible.

title: Explore guides for every shop
summary: All 21 customer-facing businesses now have setup checklists, product or service cards, supplier locations and relevant production recipes. Secondary products have their own cards and recipe sections, with business-specific equipment requirements and improved keyboard and mobile navigation.

title: Explore the game-backed Wiki
summary: Search 851 game help pages and explore a visual Gift Shop guide with setup checklists, production recipes and supplier locations. Wiki content refreshes from installed game files when the site is built. Results now lives inside Company to keep the top navigation compact.

title: Missing uniform lockers now trigger a warning
summary: Gyms and other retail businesses now warn when no Uniform Locker is installed, even if the save marks uniforms as satisfied. Gym lockers and boxed uniform lockers do not count.

title: Import deliveries count where they arrive
summary: Active importer contracts now count toward warehouse and factory supply, including new orders with no previous delivery. Mixed supply routes, paused contracts and staggered deliveries show clearer shortages and next steps.

title: See who is online and vote on what comes next
summary: An approximate online count now sits beside the green dot. Vote for Optimize staffing or Find a location from the footer, with one vote per connection IP for each feature.

title: Your rented homes, on the map
summary: A dedicated map layer shows rented homes with their addresses and daily rent, alongside your businesses and owned properties.

title: A clearer view of the city
summary: The redesigned map adds layer toggles, a floating places list, location cards and a full-screen view. Search and explore with smoother camera movement.

title: Explore your company on the map
summary: An interactive city map brings together businesses, purchased properties and searchable addresses. Location shortcuts open a map overlay without leaving your current page.

title: Factory lines get their names sooner
summary: Known recipe IDs now identify factory products immediately, so ingredient planning no longer needs delivery history. Manual naming remains available for unknown recipes.

title: Know when your previous save is loading
summary: A visible loading indicator explains when a remembered save is being restored. Clear recovery actions help when loading fails, and your previous page and selection return with your save.

title: Find saves on Windows and Mac
summary: Save help now shows a copyable path for your operating system, with a manual selector. Setup instructions are shorter and include native Steam saves on macOS.

title: More room for your dashboard
summary: The board uses the available screen width, crowded controls wrap, and repeated factory downtime sits in an expandable view. Remembered saves reopen automatically when folder access is still granted.

title: Turn supply plans into a checklist
summary: Supply Orders groups proposed quantities and estimated top-ups by location, with expandable checklists and copyable actions. Checkmarks stay in your browser as notes for changes to make in-game.

title: Better shared-ingredient planning
summary: Import planning now adds active contracts together and keeps orders needed by other product ranges. Hairdresser consumables and service fees are handled correctly in supply plans.

title: A lighter touch for the clock
summary: A subtle glow keeps the masthead clock readable as the balls roll behind it, replacing the darker background pane in both themes.

title: Smoother little interactions
summary: Masthead balls can roll behind the clock on narrower windows. Next moves cards have consistent spacing and respond promptly when you hover and tilt them.

title: Meet the redesigned Big Copilot
summary: A new look across the landing page and every dashboard view brings cleaner charts, clearer findings, detailed business cards and refined supply and growth tools, with light and dark themes.
